analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the 1803 Louisiana land transaction, its negotiators and price, Jefferson constitutional debate, later expansions toward present-day borders, sectional slavery compromises, and impact on Native peoples.

overview.headline: Louisiana Purchase bargain and its national consequences

keyPoints.point: United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million
keyPoints.quote: the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million.

keyPoints.point: negotiators Livingston and Monroe were authorized to pay up to $10 million for port of New Orleans and Floridas but agreed to entire Louisiana territory for $15 million
keyPoints.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas.

keyPoints.point: President Jefferson as strict interpreter wondered if Government authorized to acquire territory but desire to expand trumped beliefs as Napoleon threatened
keyPoints.quote: President Thomas Jefferson was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution

keyPoints.point: expansion exposed sectional weaknesses between North and South over slavery requiring fragile compromises and ignored impact on Native Americans forced onto reservations
keyPoints.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery.

keyTerms.gloss: major cession of land in long series of expansions spanning 19th century
keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase was the first major cession of land in a long series of expansions that span the 19th century.

keyTerms.gloss: Compromise aimed to maintain balance between free states and slave states
keyTerms.quote: notably the Missouri Compromise and the Compromise of 1850

keyTerms.gloss: Purchase that solidified present-day borders of contiguous United States
keyTerms.quote: present-day borders of the contiguous United States would be solidified with the Gadsden Purchase.

keyTerms.gloss: peoples whose potential impact was ignored when territories were established
keyTerms.quote: In addition, the Louisiana Purchase ignored the potential impact on Native Americans.

keyTerms.gloss: Treaty that formed Agreement with conventions regarding financial aspects
keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase Agreement is made up of the Treaty of Cession and the two conventions regarding the financial aspects of the transaction.
